+name: v2prov-ci-scopes

+description: Place new or changed v2prov provisioning tests into the CI shards in .github/scripts/provisioning-test-scopes.yaml, keeping shards balanced and path triggers accurate. Use when someone adds, renames, moves or deletes a test under tests/v2prov/tests, asks which scope or shard a test runs in, wants to rebalance provisioning CI, or edits provisioning-test-scopes.yaml.
+# v2prov CI scopes
+This skill helps a test author get their test into the right CI shard. It does five things:
+- Reads the test to work out its cost and behavior.
+- Interviews the author about anything the code can't answer.
+- Proposes edits to `.github/scripts/provisioning-test-scopes.yaml`.
+- Checks those edits mechanically before writing them.
+- Reports existing config drift separately.
+Read [reference.md](reference.md) before deciding placement. It has the scope meanings, naming tiers, cost model, hard constraints and balancing rules.

+Every path and command in this skill is relative to the repository root, so run commands from there. The scripts live in `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/`. They need `git`, `yq` (v4) and `jq`; the table output also needs `column`, and `fetch-timings.sh` needs an authenticated `gh`.

+- `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/check-coverage.sh` maps every top-level test to the rows that run it and lists problems. Use `--test <name>` for one test, `--problems` for a diffable problem list, and `--json` for raw data. `SCOPES_CONFIG=<file>` points it at a proposed copy. It exits 0 whenever the analysis ran, even if it found problems, and 2 on usage or prerequisite errors.

+- `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/fetch-timings.sh --branch <branch>` gets median per-test and per-shard durations from recent nightly runs on that branch only. Exit 3 means there's no nightly data for that branch. Warnings on stderr name any shard it couldn't map back to a nightly row; those shards are left out of the output.
+## Workflow
+### 1. Find the tests and capture a baseline
+- Work out which tests are in play. Use the names the author gives, or find new and changed top-level `func Test_` declarations in `git diff <base>...HEAD -- tests/v2prov/tests`.

+- Determine the target branch: the branch the work will merge into (the upstream tracking branch, or the PR's base). Confirm it with the author, and don't guess silently. Every timing number below is only valid for that branch.

+- Save the baseline: `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/check-coverage.sh --problems > /tmp/v2prov-baseline.txt`. Problems already in this list are pre-existing drift, not caused by the author's change.
+For each test, read the code and note:
+- **Helper and node count:** `systemdnode` (custom), `MachinePools[].Quantity` (MP), or `setUpImportedCluster` pools (imported). Also note which roles each node has.

+- **What it does:** create, scale, drain, delete, rotate certs, snapshot or restore, and so on. Note which Rancher objects it creates or asserts on (plan secrets, etcd snapshot CRs, machine objects, fleet clusters).

+- **Dist skips, env or feature gates, and `t.Parallel()`.** Compare what you read with `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/check-coverage.sh --test <name>`. The script's detection is heuristic, so trust the code when they disagree.
+- **Where it lands today**, according to the same command.
+### 2. Interview the author

+Ask the author directly. If your environment has a structured question tool (multiple choice with a free-text fallback), use it; otherwise ask in plain text with numbered options. Ask only what the code didn't settle, mark a recommended option based on what you read, and batch related questions instead of asking one at a time. Cover:

+1. **Purpose**, when the name and directory don't make it obvious. Options: first-time provisioning flow, day-2 operation, imported cluster behavior, fleet or agent behavior, or a feature-flagged path.
+2. **Exercised code.** Ask which Rancher packages or controllers this test is meant to protect.

+   - Propose candidates from what the test touches. For example, etcd snapshot CRs point to `pkg/controllers/capr/etcdmgmt/`, drain annotations to `pkg/controllers/capr/machinedrain/`, and imported day-2 ops to `pkg/controllers/capr/unmanaged/` or `pkg/operations/`.
+   - Let the author add or remove candidates.
+   - This list drives the `package-paths` edits.
+3. **Trigger scenarios.** What kind of change should make this test run? Examples: "any planner change", "changes to the snapshot restore path", "fleet version bumps".
+   - This decides PR tier versus nightly-only.
+   - It also shows whether a `file-paths` substring rule fits better than a whole package. Dependency bumps in `go.mod` and version pins in `build.yaml` or `pkg/settings/setting.go` are examples.
+4. **Distros**, if the test doesn't already restrict itself. Should it run on k3s, rke2, or both?
+5. **kdm.** Should KDM validation run it? Recommend no, unless the behavior depends on the Kubernetes version.
+6. **Runtime**, only if `fetch-timings.sh` has no data for this test. Ask how long it took locally, on which dist, and how many nodes were up at once.
+If an answer conflicts with the code, raise it rather than picking one. An example is "should run on k3s" for a test that skips on k3s.
+### 3. Decide placement
+Work through these in order:
+1. **Scope.** Pick it from the purpose and the test directory (see the scope table in reference.md).
+2. **Tier.** PR scope plus nightly, or nightly only. Apply the "Should a test run on PRs?" rules.
+3. **Name.** Check that the test name lands in the intended row.
+   - If it doesn't, propose a rename to the right prefix and Set letter before touching any regex.
+   - Renaming is almost always better than widening a regex.
+   - Run `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/fetch-timings.sh --branch <target>`.
+   - On exit 3, tell the author there's no nightly data for that branch and use the cost model in reference.md. Never borrow numbers from another branch, and never use PR runs.
+   - Pick the lightest compatible row. Only split if adding the test pushes the shard past the balancing target. Follow the split rules in reference.md, and keep rows disjoint.
+5. **Row options.** Set `V2PROV_TEST_CPUS` and `V2PROV_TEST_PARALLELISM` from node count and `t.Parallel()` usage, and `CATTLE_FEATURES` from any feature gate.
+6. **Nightly.** Make sure a nightly row covers the test on every dist it runs on in PRs, and on any extra dists it should run on nightly.
+   - Watch the 25-row cap. Nightly is close to it, so prefer widening an existing nightly row's alternation over adding a row.
+7. **kdm.** Add the test only if the author agreed.
+8. **Trigger paths.** For each package the author confirmed:
+   - If no scope lists it, add it to the chosen scope's `package-paths`, in the existing style (anchored `'^pkg/.../'`, keeping the file's grouping and alignment).
+   - If another scope already lists it, add it here too with `# also <scope>`, and update the comment on the other entry.
+   - If it's under `skip`, the author is closing a coverage gap. Move it out of `skip` and say so.
+   - If it already matches `full`, no path edit is needed.
+   - Also make sure the test's own directory is in the scope's `package-paths`.
+### 4. Propose and verify before writing
+- Copy the config to a temp file, apply the proposed edits there, then run:
+  SCOPES_CONFIG=/tmp/scopes.yaml tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/check-coverage.sh --test <name>
+  SCOPES_CONFIG=/tmp/scopes.yaml tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/check-coverage.sh --problems > /tmp/v2prov-proposed.txt
+  diff /tmp/v2prov-baseline.txt /tmp/v2prov-proposed.txt
+  The diff must not add problems. The only exception is one the author accepts knowingly. `ORPHAN-GATED` for a deliberately local-only test is an example.
+- For each new or changed trigger path, pick one real file under it and confirm the scope fires:
+  SCOPES_CONFIG=/tmp/scopes.yaml CHANGED=<file> .github/scripts/resolve-provisioning-matrix.sh
+  The stderr should name the scope, and the JSON should include the row that runs the test.
+- Show the author:
+  - The YAML diff.
+  - The rows the test will run in (PR, nightly, kdm), per dist.
+  - The change in matrix row count for the PR union and for nightly.
+  - The estimated shard time before and after, saying whether it came from nightly data (with the run IDs) or from the cost model.
+### 5. Apply

+Write the edits to the real config only after the author confirms. Then run `tests/v2prov/.agents/skills/v2prov-ci-scopes/scripts/check-coverage.sh --test <name>` and the `--problems` diff against the baseline once more.
+### 6. Report pre-existing drift
+Split the baseline problems that aren't related to this change into two groups:
+- **Known drift**, listed in reference.md. Mention it once, and don't offer fixes.
+- **Everything else** is new drift. Offer a fix for each problem, and apply only the fixes the author picks. Keep them as separate edits so they can go in their own commit.
+## Rules
+- Never widen a regex to `.*` or a bare prefix just to catch one test.
+- Never let two rows in one scope match the same test on the same dist.
+- Never edit the workflows, the resolver or `scripts/provisioning-tests` as part of placing a test. If a constraint there is the real blocker, say so.
+- Keep the YAML's existing alignment, quoting and comment style.
+- Row keys pass straight through to the matrix. When splitting or copying a row, carry over every key it has, including ones this repo doesn't read (such as `V2PROV_TEST_RUN_ON_RELEASE`).
+- When removing or renaming a test, check that no row becomes dead (`DEAD-ROW`) and that no enumerated alternation still lists the old name.
+# v2prov CI scopes reference

+Background for placing tests in `.github/scripts/provisioning-test-scopes.yaml`. The header comment in that file and in `.github/scripts/resolve-provisioning-matrix.sh` are the source of truth for the config format. This file covers the conventions and constraints that aren't written there.
+## How a PR picks its tests
+1. `resolve-provisioning-matrix.sh` diffs the PR against its base.
+2. A changed file that matches a `full` entry selects every scope under `scopes`.
+3. Otherwise each scope whose `package-paths` (or `file-paths`, with optional substring rules) match a changed file is selected.
+4. The selected scopes' `tests` rows become the GHA matrix, one job per row per dist.

+Row keys are the environment variable names the workflow reads (`V2PROV_TEST_DIST`, `V2PROV_TEST_RUN_REGEX`, `CATTLE_FEATURES`, `V2PROV_TEST_CPUS`, `V2PROV_TEST_PARALLELISM`, `V2PROV_TEST_TIMEOUT`, `V2PROV_RUNNER_FAMILY`). The resolver passes every key on a row through to the matrix unchanged, then fills in defaults for dist (both), cpus (16) and parallelism (1). Any scope, PR or explicit, can set `meta.V2PROV_TEST_TIMEOUT` and `meta.V2PROV_RUNNER_FAMILY` as defaults for its rows; a row that sets the same key keeps its own value. Keys this repo doesn't read are still passed through. For example, kdm rows set `V2PROV_TEST_RUN_ON_RELEASE`, which is for downstream consumers. Keep such keys on any row you edit or split, and copy them onto new rows in the same scope. Every key also shows up in the GHA job name, so don't add keys just for documentation.

+`explicit` scopes (`nightly`, `kdm`) are never picked by a diff, not even with `ALL=1`. They only run when requested by name. So a test can sit in a PR scope and in nightly at the same time without running twice.
+## Scopes
+| Scope | Purpose | Test dirs |
+| `basic` | general, custom and machine provisioning, fleet, agent | `general/`, `custom/`, `machineprovisioning/`, `fleet/`, `autoscaler/` |
+| `operations` | day-2 ops (cert rotation, encryption key rotation, etcd snapshot, drain) on custom and MP clusters | `custom/`, `machineprovisioning/` |
+| `imported` | imported cluster lifecycle and day-2 ops | `imported/` |
+| `prebootstrap` | prebootstrap secrets flow, on both dists | `prebootstrap/` |
+| `full` (paths only) | core code where any change can break all provisioning: planner, plan, rkecontrolplane, rkecluster, the v2prov framework, the runner | n/a |
+| `skip` (paths only) | provisioning-related code with no v2prov coverage, listed so nobody adds it to a scope by accident | n/a |
+| `nightly` (explicit) | everything that should run on merged code, once per day per listed branch | all |
+| `kdm` (explicit) | subset run when validating KDM data changes (new k8s versions) | k8s-version-sensitive tests |
+A package can appear in more than one scope. The file marks this with a trailing `# also <scope>` comment; keep that convention.
+## Naming and tiers
+The test name decides which row picks it up. Prefer giving a test the right name over widening a regex to catch it.
+| Prefix | Where it runs |

+| `Test_General_*` | basic (rke2 only, and only the names its row enumerates, so a new `General` test needs adding there), nightly (rke2 only). `Test_General_PreBootstrap_*` runs in the `prebootstrap` scope on both dists instead of basic, plus a k3s nightly row |
+| `Test_Fleet_*` | basic (rke2 only), nightly (rke2 only) |
+| `Test_Provisioning_SetA_*`, `Test_Provisioning_Custom_SetA_*` | basic (both dists), nightly, kdm |
+| `Test_Provisioning_SetB_*`, `Test_Provisioning_Custom_SetB_*` | nightly and kdm only |
+| `Test_Operation_SetA_*` | operations (both), nightly, kdm |
+| `Test_Operation_SetB_*` | operations (k3s in one row; rke2 split across several rows, see the config), nightly, kdm |
+| `Test_Operation_SetC_*` | operations (k3s only), nightly (k3s only), kdm (both dists, since kdm rows set no dist) |
+| `Test_Imported_Operation_SetD_*` | imported, but only the tests named explicitly in its rows; nightly lists most of the rest by name |
+| `Test_Imported_Operation_SetE_*` | nightly only (heavy multi-node restore work) |

+For provisioning tests, SetA is the cheap PR tier and SetB is nightly-only. For operations, the letters are shard buckets, not tiers. In imported, SetD rows enumerate names, so adding a SetD test always means editing a row.
+`MP` in a name means machine provisioning (pod-backed machines via `nodeconfig`). `Custom` means custom clusters (`systemdnode` pods joined with the registration command).
+## Should a test run on PRs?
+Put it in a PR scope only if all of these hold:
+- It guards code that changes often enough that a regression should block a merge.
+- No PR-tier test already exercises the same path. If one does, the new test goes nightly-only.
+- It doesn't depend on env that PR CI doesn't provide (for example `V2PROV_TEST_CAPRKE2`, a dual-stack host).
+Otherwise it goes in nightly only. Every test that runs on PRs must also run in nightly, for each dist it runs on in PRs.

+kdm is for behavior that changes with the Kubernetes version: etcd snapshot and restore, cert rotation, encryption key rotation, basic provisioning. Default to not adding a test to kdm unless the author says it covers something like that.
+## Cost model
+- Every cluster node is a pod on one host cluster, on one runner. Cost is roughly node count times wall time.
+- Node count by helper:
+  - Custom: one `systemdnode.New(...)` per node.
+  - MP: `RKEConfig.MachinePools[].Quantity` (defaults to `nodeconfig.NewPodConfig`).
+  - Imported: the `[]cluster.ImportedNodePool{...Quantity}` passed to `setUpImportedCluster`.

+- `go test -p 3` (`V2PROV_PACKAGE_PARALLELISM`) already runs up to three packages at once. A row matching tests in `custom/` and `machineprovisioning/` runs those concurrently whatever `V2PROV_TEST_PARALLELISM` says.
+- `V2PROV_TEST_PARALLELISM` becomes `go test -parallel`. It only affects tests that call `t.Parallel()`. Setting it on a row where no test does is a no-op.

+- `V2PROV_TEST_CPUS` only picks the runner label (`runner=<cpus>cpu-linux-x64`). Default is 16. The imported rows that run 1-node tests one at a time use 8. Larger multi-node or parallel rows need 16.
+- `-failfast` is on: one failure stops the rest of that shard. Smaller shards fail more precisely.

+- Runner disk matters. A row runs on c7i-flex with EBS unless it or its scope's `meta` sets `V2PROV_RUNNER_FAMILY` (c6id gives local NVMe). Check the config for which rows set one; nightly's meta currently doesn't (see the comment there). The imported etcd tests are limited by disk writes and run about 25% faster on NVMe. `fetch-timings.sh` reports each shard's `family`, so compare timings from the same family, and scale them when the target row runs on the other one.
+When nightly timing data isn't available for the target branch, estimate with node count and the closest existing test, and say so to the author.
+## Hard constraints

+- **Regex characters.** `scripts/provisioning-tests` rejects any regex outside `^[][A-Za-z0-9_()|.^$*?]+$`. Character classes and `?` are allowed. No `+`, `{}`, `-`, spaces or `\`. Prefer alternation of full names when it reads more clearly.
+- **No lookahead.** Go uses RE2. To carve a test out of a `.*` row, enumerate the rest by name or rename tests so the prefixes separate.
+- **No overlap.** Rows in one scope must match disjoint tests for the same dist. Across PR scopes this also matters, since several scopes can fire on one PR and the resolver doesn't de-duplicate.

+- **Timeouts.** Rows get the 60m `go test` default unless the row or its scope's `meta` sets `V2PROV_TEST_TIMEOUT` (`^[0-9]+[mh]$`, e.g. `200m` or `5h`; `check-coverage.sh` reports `INVALID-TIMEOUT` otherwise). PR scopes currently don't set one. The GHA job is capped at 360m including setup.

+- **Matrix cap.** `provisioning-tests.yml` fails if the matrix has more than 25 entries. Count expanded rows: a row with no `V2PROV_TEST_DIST` counts twice. A `full` trigger runs the union of all PR scopes, so their combined row count must also stay at or under 25.

+- **Artifact names.** Each job uploads `Test Results <dist> <suite>`, where `<suite>` is the regex with `Test` removed and `[]()|_^.*$?` stripped. Two rows in the same run with the same dist and suite overwrite each other.
+- **New scopes.** A new scope needs a `'^trigger-<scope>-ci$'` file-paths entry and must be added to the scope choices in `.github/workflows/ci-testing-create-pr.yml`.
+## Balancing
+- Target: a shard's `Run tests` step should stay under about 70% of its timeout (about 40m for PR rows).
+- Add to the lightest compatible row first: same scope, same dist set, same `CATTLE_FEATURES`, compatible `V2PROV_TEST_CPUS`.
+- Split a row only when adding the test would push it past the target. Split by adding a new row that is mutually exclusive with the old one:
+  - Prefer a name-based split (move tests to a new Set letter or a distinct name fragment).
+  - Otherwise enumerate names in an alternation, as the imported rows do.
+- A test that calls `t.Parallel()` can share a row with other parallel tests if `V2PROV_TEST_PARALLELISM` is raised. That only helps if the runner has the CPU for the extra nodes.
+- When splitting a PR row, check whether the matching nightly row needs the same split. Nightly rows run on a 200m timeout, so they can usually absorb more.
+## Known drift (as of 2026-11)
+`check-coverage.sh` reports these. They are known and accepted for now. Mention them to the author once per session, don't offer to fix them, and don't count them against a proposed change:
+- **Dead path.** `full` lists `^pkg/controllers/provisioningv2/rke2/`, which matches no tracked file (`DEAD-PATH`).

+- **Orphans.** `Test_Autoscaling_Provisioning`, the `ImportedServerJoinOutsideCertificateSANs` and `StaleAddressOutsideLeaderCertificate` SetD tests, `...LocalHAIPv6`, and the six `CAPRKE2Docker*` SetE tests match no row. The CAPRKE2 and IPv6 tests are deliberately local-only.
+- **Nightly is near the cap.** It isn't reported as a problem, but `check-coverage.sh` prints the current count under "Matrix capacity". Check it before adding a nightly row.
+Anything else the script reports that isn't caused by the author's change is new drift. Offer a fix, and apply it only if the author agrees.
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Reports how every top-level v2prov test maps onto the rows in
+# provisioning-test-scopes.yaml, and flags configuration problems.
+# Usage:
+#   check-coverage.sh                 full placement table + problems
+#   check-coverage.sh --test <name>   placement for one test + problems
+#   check-coverage.sh --problems      problems only (stable, sorted, diffable)
+#   check-coverage.sh --json          raw analysis as JSON
+# SCOPES_CONFIG overrides the config path, so a proposed edit can be checked
+# from a temp copy before it is written to the real file.
+# Dist skips, t.Parallel() and env/feature gates are detected statically from
+# the test body and the same-package helpers it calls (up to 3 levels deep).
+# This is a heuristic: always read the test before trusting a skip flag.
+# Exit status: 0 when the analysis ran, whether or not it found problems (pre-existing
+# drift is normal, so compare --problems output against a baseline instead), 2 on usage
+# or prerequisite errors.
+set -uo pipefail
+ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "error: not inside a git checkout" >&2; exit 2; }
+CONFIG="${SCOPES_CONFIG:-$ROOT/.github/scripts/provisioning-test-scopes.yaml}"
+TESTS_DIR="$ROOT/tests/v2prov/tests"
+# Mirrors the whitelist in scripts/provisioning-tests and the cap in
+# .github/workflows/provisioning-tests.yml.
+REGEX_WHITELIST='^[][A-Za-z0-9_()|.^$*?]+$'
+MATRIX_CAP=25
+# Mirrors the V2PROV_TEST_TIMEOUT check in scripts/provisioning-tests.
+TIMEOUT_FORMAT='^[0-9]+[mh]$'
+MODE=table
+TEST_NAME=""
+# require_value exits with a usage error when flag has no value after it. Without this,
+# 'shift 2' on the last argument fails without shifting and the parse loop never ends.
+require_value() {
+  local flag="$1"
+  local remaining="$2"
+  if [ "$remaining" -lt 2 ]; then
+    echo "error: $flag requires a value" >&2
+    exit 2
+  fi
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --test)     require_value "$1" "$#"; TEST_NAME="$2"; MODE=test; shift 2 ;;
+    --problems) MODE=problems; shift ;;
+    --json)     MODE=json; shift ;;
+    *)          echo "error: unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+if [ "$MODE" = test ] && [ -z "$TEST_NAME" ]; then
+  echo "error: --test requires a test name" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
